title: On spectral properties of Generalized Kadanoff--Baym Ansatz
abstract: The Generalized Kadanoff--Baym Ansatz with mean-field propagators is increasingly used to simulate non-equilibrium quantum fermionic and bosonic systems. Compared with the full Kadanoff--Baym equations, its mean-field propagators substantially reduce computational cost, enabling simulations with computational effort that scales linearly with propagation time. However, the time-diagonal structure of the Generalized Kadanoff--Baym Ansatz obscures spectral properties within the collision integral of the transport equation. Here, we recover and investigate these hidden spectral properties using the extended Generalized Kadanoff--Baym Ansatz. For a Hubbard cluster, we compare ground-state spectral functions obtained with the extended Generalized Kadanoff--Baym Ansatz against those from standard Kadanoff--Baym equations. At moderate interaction strengths, the spectral functions show good agreement. At large interaction strengths, however, significant deviations emerge, and the spectral function obtained with the extended Generalized Kadanoff--Baym Ansatz becomes negative. These results demonstrate that, despite its computational advantages, the Generalized Kadanoff--Baym Ansatz has important limitations in strongly interacting regimes and may produce unphysical spectral properties when interactions become sufficiently large.
summary: This work analyzes the spectral properties of the Generalized Kadanoff--Baym Ansatz (GKBA) used to simulate strongly correlated quantum systems like the Hubbard model. While the GKBA offers significant computational speed-ups, the authors demonstrate that at large interaction strengths, the approximation breaks down, leading to unphysical results such as negative spectral functions. This highlights a critical trade-off between computational tractability and physical accuracy in non-equilibrium many-body theory.
main_problem: The paper investigates the spectral properties hidden within the collision integral of the Generalized Kadanoff--Baym Ansatz (GKBA) when simulating non-equilibrium quantum fermionic systems.
main_result: At large interaction strengths, the spectral function obtained using the extended GKBA becomes negative, indicating that the GKBA has significant limitations and may yield unphysical results in strongly correlated regimes.
method: The authors compare results from the full Kadanoff--Baym Equations (KBE) against approximations derived from the GKBA and its extension (eGKBA), utilizing mean-field Hartree-Fock approximations.
model_or_system: The study uses a Hubbard cluster (or Hubbard ring model) as the physical system, governed by a Hamiltonian involving hopping and on-site interaction terms.
key_observables: Single-particle spectral functions, single-particle density matrix, and the single-particle Green's function components.
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($U$), which is varied from moderate to large values to test the stability of the approximation.
main_assumptions: The primary approximation is the use of the GKBA, which truncates reconstruction equations for computational efficiency, leading to the Hartree-Fock-GKBA (HF-GKBA).
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the spectral functions obtained from KBE and HF-eGKBA for varying interaction strengths U, showing deviations and negativity for large U.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the GKBA as a computationally cheaper alternative to KBE, then develops the extended version (eGKBA). The core of the work involves comparing the spectral properties of the eGKBA against the full KBE, culminating in the demonstration of unphysical negative spectral weights at strong coupling.
why_interesting: The findings directly address the reliability of advanced non-equilibrium simulation techniques (like GKBA) when applied to strongly correlated materials, providing crucial theoretical warnings about the limits of computational approximations.
